rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains arayta as an attention-getting question meaning consider or tell me what you think; it usually rebukes, admonishes, or expresses amazement rather than seeking information.
rows.anchor: Onun için biz de yerine göre “gördün mü? Ne dersin? Söyle bakalım! Baksan a” diye terceme edegeldik.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three questions may all address the Prophet or humanity, or alternate between disputants; the author finds the turn-taking debate more meaningful, though the first clearly addresses the Prophet and extends to everyone.
rows.anchor: tarafeyn beyninde bir muhakeme veya bir hitâbet üslûbuyla sağa sola telvîn-i hitab olmak da kābil ve daha mânalıdır

rows.speaker: İbn Atıyye
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says exegetes agree that the praying servant is the Messenger and the person forbidding him is Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: İbn Atıyye’nin beyânına göre burada namaz kılan bir abdden murad Resûlullah, nehyeden de Ebû Cehil olduğunda müfessirîn ihtilâf etmemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from recitation to prayer is apt because recitation is a prayer pillar and prayer is the foundation of worship and pillar of religion; this shows the verses came after prayer was legislated.
rows.anchor: Kıraatten bahsolunurken namaza geçilmesi onda kıraatin bir rükün olması

rows.speaker: Ebû Hüreyre
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Abu Jahl swore by Lat and Uzza to trample and soil the Prophet’s face if he saw him pray; approaching, he recoiled, describing a fiery trench, terror, and wings, and the Prophet said angels would tear him apart.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hüreyre’den rivayetlerinde: Ebû Cehil Resûlullah’ı namaz kılarken görürse muhakkak boynunu çiğneyip yüzünü sürteceğine dair

rows.speaker: Tirmizî
rows.claim: Tirmidhi’s version has Abu Jahl approach the praying Prophet, repeating that he had forbidden him to do this.
rows.anchor: Tirmizî’nin rivayetinde de [5957] Peygamber namaz kılarken Ebû Cehil

rows.speaker: Hasan
rows.claim: The author rejects Hasan’s report that Umayya forbade Salman to pray: Salman embraced Islam in Medina after the Hijra, whereas the sura is agreed to be Meccan.
rows.anchor: Hasan’dan mervî olan rivayet sahih olamaz. Çünkü Selman’ın islâmı hicretten sonra Medine’de olduğunda hilâf bulunmadığı gibi, sûrenin Mekkî olduğunda da hilâf yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the occasion concerned Abu Jahl, the verse’s general ruling also covers anyone like Bilal who is stopped from prayer.
rows.anchor: âyetin hükmü âm olduğu için ona ve emsâline de şâmil olacağında şüphe yoktur

rows.speaker: Tebrizî
rows.claim: Tabrizi reports that salat here meant the noon prayer, the first congregational prayer in Islam, performed by Abu Bakr, Ali, and early Muslims when Abu Talib arrived with Ja‘far and urged him to join them.
rows.anchor: Tebrizî demiş ki: “Burada ‘salât’tan murad öğle namazıdır

rows.speaker: Ebû Tâlib
rows.claim: In verses cited by Tabrizi, Abu Talib declares he will not abandon the Prophet and urges Ali and Ja‘far to support their cousin.
rows.anchor: Ebû Tâlib şu beyitleri söylüyordu: إِنَّ عَلِيًّا وَجَعْفَرًا ثِقَتِ ي عِنْدَ مُلِمِّ الزَّمَانِ وَالْكُرَ بِ وَاللّٰهَِّ لاَ أَخْذُلُ النَّبِيَّ

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi objects that prayer became obligatory only on the Night Journey, which he places after Abu Talib’s death; he cites chronologies placing Isra one to five years before the Hijra and Abu Talib’s death three years before it.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî der ki: “Bunda nazar vardır. Çünkü namaz hiç hilâfsız İsrâ gecesinde farz kılınmıştır. İsrâ’ın hicretten bir sene evvel olduğuna da İbn Hazm icmâ‘iddia etmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds Alusi’s objection unpersuasive: Isra established the five daily prayers, while earlier legislation of other prayers, such as night vigil or a noon prayer, remains possible.
rows.anchor: Çünkü İsrâ’da farz kılınan mutlak namaz değil, beş vakit namazdır. Binâen‘aleyh ondan evvel Müzzemmil’de geçtiği vechile gece kıyâmının farz olması gibi bir öğle namazının da farz kılınmış olmasına münâfî olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited account calls it the noon prayer without explicitly saying it was obligatory; the prayer said to have first been performed publicly after Umar’s conversion was likely this one.
rows.anchor: mezkur rivayette salât-i zuhr denilmiş, farz olduğu tasrih de olunmamıştır. Hazret-i Ömer’in islâmı üzerine ilk olarak alenen kılındığı rivayet olunan namaz da bu olmak gerektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the occasion involved noon prayer, the unrestricted verse covers forbidding any legally prescribed or voluntary prayer, since the prohibition targets prayer itself.
rows.anchor: âyette de murad yalnız odur demek doğru olmaz. Çünkü âyet mutlaktır. Meşrû‘olan herhangi bir namaza şâmildir. Gerek farz ve gerek nâfile herhangi bir namazdan nehiy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prohibition due to an accompanying circumstance such as a disliked time or usurped place differs, because it concerns time or place rather than prayer itself.
rows.anchor: Meğer ki esâs-ı nehy namazın kendisinden değil de ahvâl-i mukārinesinden biri itibariyle olsun o vakit câiz olabilir

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
rows.claim: Ali saw people praying before the Eid prayer and said he had not seen the Messenger do that; when asked why he did not forbid them, he feared falling under this threat.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ali kerremallahu vecheh musallâda bayram namazından evvel namaz kılan bazı kimseleri gördüğü zaman “Resûlullah’ı böyle yaparken görmedim” demiş

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
rows.claim: In another report, Ali says he does not wish to forbid a person from praying, but will tell them what he saw the Messenger do.
rows.anchor: Diğer bir rivayette de “bir kulu namaz kılarken nehyetmeyi arzu [5959] etmem

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa answers Abu Yusuf’s question about a supplication after bowing by prescribing “Our Lord, praise belongs to You,” without explicitly forbidding the alternative, illustrating caution about prohibition.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe rahmetullahi aleyh Hazretleri, kendisine İmam Ebû Yûsuf “musallî rükûdan başını kaldırırken اَللّٰهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي der mi?” diye sorduğu zaman

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forbidding other acts of worship is analogous to forbidding prayer; verbal prohibition and stopping someone through conduct are alike, so distracting someone from worship also falls under the threat, as with Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: Sâir ibadetlerden nehiy de namazdan nehye kıyas olunur. Bu babda kavlen nehy ile fiilen ve hâlen nehiy arasında fark da yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional sentence has an omitted consequence, and the pronouns in “was upon guidance” and “commanded piety” may refer either to the servant or to the prohibitor, shifting the addressee accordingly.
rows.anchor: bu kaziyye şartiyye olduğundan cezâsı mahzuftur. كَانَ، اَمَرَ zamirleri “abd”e de nehyedene de râci‘olabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the pronouns refer to the praying servant, the address turns to the tyrant: would it be bad if the servant followed truth or urged others to fear God and avoid evil?
rows.anchor: “Düşünsene ey namaz kılan bir kulu nehyeden azgın insan! Eğer o kul hidâyet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the pronouns refer to the prohibitor, the address remains with the worshipper: how much better if the prohibitor followed guidance or urged piety instead of stopping prayer?
rows.anchor: Nehyedene râci‘olduğu takdirde ise hitab, yine evvelki siyakta olarak “abd”e müteveccih olup

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing the Prophet, the question asks whether it is good for the prohibitor to deny the truth and turn away while the Prophet speaks truly.
rows.anchor: Peygamber’e hitab olduğuna göre şöyle demek olur: Baksana, yahut gördün a yâ Muhammed! Sen doğru olduğun, hakkı söylediğin hâlde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing the prohibitor, the alternative reading asks whether it would be good for the servant to obey him by denying truth, abandoning prayer, and turning away.
rows.anchor: Baksana, ey o kulu namazdan nehyeden azgın!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees right and wrong, good and evil, and will repay everyone according to their deeds.
rows.anchor: Sonra kendisine varılacak olan Allah her hâlde doğruyu da eğriyi de, iyiyi de kötüyü de hepsini görür ve herkesin ameline göre cezâsını verir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “does he not know” can refer to either interlocutor: the servant knows God sees all and will not obey, or the prohibitor is asked whether he still fails to know; both readings threaten him.
rows.anchor: Hitab nâhiye olduğu surette “abd”e râci‘olup istifhâm-ı inkârî olarak: “O kul Allah’ın hepsini gördüğünü bilir. Senin nehyini dinlemez ey azgın!” demek olur

rows.speaker: Keşşâf
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf allows both conditional clauses to have expressed consequences, but the author prefers treating them as omitted and the following statement as an independent resumption.
rows.anchor: Keşşâf’ın dediği gibi iki şartın ikisinin de cevâbı yapmak câiz olsa bile şartların cezâları mahzuf olarak bunun bir cümle-i istînâfiye olması daha muvâfıktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rejects and warns against the tyrant’s conduct.
rows.anchor: O azgının hâlinden red‘[^16] u tahzirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasiyah means the hair or forelock on the forehead and can also name the forehead or front of the head; here it is a metonym for the head and therefore the person.
rows.anchor: “Nâsıye” mâlum ki alındaki saç, perçem demektir. Onun bittiği cebheye, alına, yani alnın üstünde başın ön tarafına dahi ıtlak olunur. Burada murad baştan ve dolayısıyla şahıstan kinayedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite apposition generalizes the threat; “lying, sinful” both justifies the dragging and clarifies that the person, who actually lies and sins, is meant, though the literal forelock remains possible too.
rows.anchor: Yalancı, hatîekâr; cânî bir nâsıyeyi bu bedelin nekre olarak getirilmesi emsâline ta‘mîm içindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadi derives from nadwa, a gathering for discussion; the pre-Islamic Quraysh meeting hall was Dar al-Nadwa, and the word names the assembled body, like an assembly, congress, or parliament, so “kurultay” suits contemporary Turkish.
rows.anchor: “bezm”, “meclis”, “mahfil”, “kongre”, “parlaman” tâbirleri gibidir

rows.speaker: Tirmizî
rows.claim: Tirmidhi reports Abu Jahl’s boast that he had the majority of the assembly on his side; the verse points to this boast and answers that God will summon the Zabaniya.
rows.anchor: Tirmizî’de [5962] de rivayet olunduğu üzere Ebû Cehil, nâdîce ekseriyet kendisinin olduğunu söylediği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zabaniya names the punishment angels; lexicographers say the original word meant police or security forces, with disagreement over whether it has a singular form or derives from zabn, repelling.
rows.anchor: “Zebânî”, “Zebâniye” azab melâikelerine isim olmuştur. Demişlerdir ki asıl lügatta şurta, yani zâbıta kuvveti demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The summons of these angels implies that the lying, sinful person will be dragged into Hell.
rows.anchor: Bu zebânîlerin davetinden anlaşılır ki o yalancı, cânî nâsıye cehenneme sürüklenecektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated warning means not to heed the arrogant liar who forbids prayer, but to obey the Lord, continue reciting, and prostrate.
rows.anchor: Ona itaat etme öyle müstağnî yalancı, cânî, namazdan nehyeder azgını dinleme

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sound hadith says the servant is closest to the Lord while prostrating; a qudsi hadith says continued voluntary worship draws the servant near until God guides his hearing, sight, and heart.
rows.anchor: kulun rabbine en yakın olabileceği hâl secde ederkendir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prostration may mean prayer in light of the earlier reference, but its literal sense is more apparent because “draw near” already covers prayer and other worship; separately naming prostration stresses its importance as perfect humility and submission.
rows.anchor: Burada “secde” yukarıdaki salât karînesiyle namaz mânasına olmak dahi muhtemil ise de hakikati üzere bilhassa kendi mânasında olmak daha zâhirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two Sahih collections establish that the Prophet performed recitation prostration in both Surat al-Inshiqaq and this sura; the author urges readers to prostrate and keep drawing near to God.
rows.anchor: Sahîheyn’de sâbit olduğu üzere Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm اِذَا السَّمَٓاءُ انْشَقَّتْ’da ve bu sûrede tilâvet secdesi yapmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun “it” means the recited Quran: God sent it down in His majesty, so the command is to recite and worship Him; the majestic plural honors both sender and revelation.
rows.anchor: Elhak Biz indirdik onu yani oku da ancak Bize secde ve ibadet et, çünkü şân-ı azametimizle Biz indirdik onu; o okunan Kur’ân’ı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic nominal-verbal construction repeats the divine subject as both topic and agent, packing in two judgments; with the nominal sentence, repeated attribution, and inna, it gives triple emphasis and may convey restriction.
rows.anchor: müsned-i ileyh olan mütekellim zamiri نا bir mübtedâ bir de fâil olarak tekerrür etmiş

rows.speaker: cumhûr-ı müfessirîn
rows.claim: The majority of exegetes take the pronoun “it” to refer to the Quran; Bukhari likewise identifies the pronoun as an allusion to the Quran.
rows.anchor: cumhûr-ı müfessirîn Kur’ân’a râci‘dir demişlerdir. Buhârî’de mezkur olan da “hâ” Kur’an’dan kinayedir

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi says exegetes unanimously refer the pronoun to the Quran, while views naming Gabriel or another referent are not a substantive disagreement; Shihab deems such alternatives weak because Gabriel’s descent entails the Quran’s descent.
rows.anchor: Râzî bunda müfessirînin icmâ‘ını söylemiş

rows.speaker: Hattâbî
rows.claim: Alusi transmits al-Khattabi’s view that the pronoun points to God’s command “Read,” explaining why this sura follows the first revelation; Ibn al-Arabi calls the idea remarkable.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî’nin naklettiği vechile Hattâbî إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ zamiri Allah teâlâ’nın اِقْرَأْ kavline işaret olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Referring the pronoun to “Read” does not really oppose the majority, since that command was the first Quran revealed; it also makes the referent explicit from the preceding sura and avoids construing “sending down” as beginning revelation.
rows.anchor: اِقْرَأْ Kur’ân’ın ilk nâzil olan âyeti olduğu cihetle onun inzâli Kur’ân’ın indirilmeye başlaması demek olacağı cihetle zamirin ona ircâ‘ı da hakikatte cumhur kavline muhalif olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the sura is Medinan, the pronoun could refer to the promised seizure in the previous sura, fulfilled at Badr; the allusion would resemble Quran 8:41, and “day” can include the night when the victory began.
rows.anchor: Bu surette Ebû Cehl’in o yalancı, cânî kafasının kesilip cehenneme doğru sürüklendiği Bedir nusretinin nüzûlüne işaret olarak وَمَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَىٰ عَبْدِنَا يَوْمَ ٱلْفُرْقَانِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Badr reading could connect the night to Ramadan 17, when Badr occurred; Hasan reports that Night of Decree was then, but this reading conflicts with reports locating it in the last ten nights, especially the 27th, and with a Meccan sura.
rows.anchor: leyle-i kadir ramazanın on yedinci gecesi olduğu, çünkü Bedir Vak‘ası onun sabahında vukū‘bulduğu Hasan’dan da rivayet edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The strongest reports suggest the Night of Decree is concealed, sought especially in Ramadan’s last ten nights and particularly the 27th; Badr was one such night that year, not the only Night of Decree.
rows.anchor: en sağlam rivayet mülâhaza edilince kadir gecesi Bedir Gecesi’nden ibaret demek değil, lâkin Bedir Gecesi kadir gecelerinden biri idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clearest, mutually agreed meaning is that the pronoun refers generally to all or part of the Quran, while “Read” and Badr remain plausible included possibilities.
rows.anchor: en kat‘î ve müttefekun aleyh olan mâna, zamirin kül veya ba‘z mutlak Kur’ân’a ircâ‘ıdır

rows.speaker: İkrime
rows.claim: A report transmitted from Ibn Abbas through Ikrima says the whole Quran descended together to the lowest heaven on the Night of Decree, then was revealed from there as God willed until it was collected.
rows.anchor: İkrime’den: Kur’an hepsi bir cümle olarak ramazanda leyle-i kadirde dünyâ semâya indi

rows.speaker: Hakîm b. Cübeyr
rows.claim: A report transmitted from Ibn Abbas through Hakim ibn Jubayr says the Quran descended all at once from the highest to the lowest heaven and was then divided over the years; Ibn Abbas cited Quran 56:75 and said it came in parts.
rows.anchor: Hakîm b. Cübeyr’den: Kur’an bir gecede semâ-i ulyâdan semâ-i dünyâya cümle-i vâhide olarak indi

rows.speaker: Sa‘îd b. Cübeyr
rows.claim: A report says the Quran descended whole to the lowest heaven on the Night of Decree and was then sent to the Messenger gradually; Ibn Abbas cited Quran 25:32 for this staged revelation.
rows.anchor: Sa‘îd b. Cübeyr’den: “Kur’an cümle-i vâhide olarak leyle-i Kadir’de semâ-i dünyâya indi

rows.speaker: Aynî
rows.claim: Ayni’s account has the Quran descend whole from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven and Bayt al-Izza on the Night of Decree; Gabriel dictated it to scribes, then delivered it gradually to the Prophet over 23 years.
rows.anchor: Aynî’nin Buhârî şerhinde ifadesine göre cümle-i vâhide olarak leyle-i kadirde Levh-i Mahfûz’dan semâ-i dünyâya indirildi de Beyt-i İzzet’e kondu

rows.speaker: Şa‘bî
rows.claim: One report from Sha‘bi says it reached them that the whole Quran descended all at once to the lowest heaven.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr’de Şa‘bî’den de iki rivayet vardır:

rows.speaker: Şa‘bî
rows.claim: A second report from Sha‘bi says the beginning of the Quran descended on the Night of Decree.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın evveli leyle-i kadirde indi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes mainly follow two readings: the pronoun refers to the whole Quran and “sending down” means a complete descent, or it refers to the beginning and means the start of revelation; referring it to “Read” makes the latter plain.
rows.anchor: Onun için tefsirlerde başlıca bu iki vecih üzere yürümüşlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since Quranic “sending down” can mean manifestation from the unseen to the visible world, it can also describe fulfillment of a foretold event or promise, including the promised seizure at Badr.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’a nisbet olunan “inzâl”in mânası Sûre-i Bakara’nın başında da geçtiği üzere âlem-i gaybden âlem-i şehâdete izhar[^16]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although some interpret “in the Night of Decree” as “about the Night” by ellipsis or causal reading, the author prefers the direct locative sense; otherwise the Quran’s revelation, the night’s greatest distinction, is left unstated and the sura’s links to its context weaken.
rows.anchor: Fakat bu âyeti buna hamletmek nâkıstır. Zira doğrudan doğru zarfiyet mümkin iken sebebiyete veya hazf-i muzâfa gitmek hilâf-ı zâhir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Qadr” derives from a root meaning ability and can mean decree, determination, honor, majesty, or constriction; Razi says qadr and qadar match in meaning, with one form a verbal noun and the other a noun.
rows.anchor: “Kadr” قدر يقدر fiilinin masdarı olarak esası güç yetirmek demek olup hükm ü kazâ, takdir, şeref ü azamet ve tazyik mânalarına gelir

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: Mujahid, as cited by Ibn Jarir, interprets the Night of Decree as the night of judgment, when decisive matters are separated, as described in Quran 44:3–4; most exegetes identify that blessed night with this one.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr’in Mücâhid’den naklettiği vechile hüküm gecesi demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because eternal determination is already made, “decree” here means its disclosure and execution; the verse’s “separated” wording supports this. Although some constrain it to one year’s lifespans and provisions, the wording encompasses important matters over many years and eras.
rows.anchor: burada murad o hüküm ve takdîrin izhar ve infâzı ile hüküm ve kazâ olmak lâzım gelir. Âyette يُفْرَقُ buyurulması da buna delâlet eyler

rows.speaker: Zührî
rows.claim: Zuhri interprets qadr as honor and majesty, like the Turkish expression “kadr ü haysiyet”; the night is thus a night of great honor.
rows.anchor: Zührî’den mervî olduğu üzere “kadr” bizim de “kadr ü haysiyet” tâbir ettiğimiz vechile şeref ve azamet mânasına olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is constriction: the angels crowd the earth that night; the author relates this to the pressure that accompanies events whose eventual good and deliverance are immense, as revelation began with an angel’s intense pressure.
rows.anchor: tazyik mânasına olmasıdır ki tazyik gecesi demek olur. Zira o gece inen melâikeye Arz dar gelir denilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All three senses—decree, honor, and constriction—apply together; the title’s three repetitions in the sura hint at this.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde “leyle-i kadir”de bu üç mânanın üçü de var demektir. Bu sûrede لَيْلَةِ ٱلْقَدْرِ unvânının üç defa zikredilmiş olması da buna bir işarettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means the night is too great for unaided human insight to grasp; God makes its nature and rank known, and the phrase can also be rendered “Do you know what the Night of Decree is?”
rows.anchor: o kadir gecesi öyle büyük bir gecedir ki sırf senin kendi dirayetine kalsa idi onun mâhiyetini, kadrinin derecesini bilemezdin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship, good works, and striving on that night earn more good and reward than a thousand months without it; the benefit is beyond a fixed measure, known fully only to God.
rows.anchor: O gece amel ve ibadet ve mücahede ile erilecek olan hayr ü sevab, onsuz bin ay amel ile kazanılacak olan hayr ü sevabdan daha çok

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Night of Decree’s gift of immeasurable reward is a special favor to Muhammad and his community.
rows.anchor: Bu mahza Allah teâlâ’nın Muhammed ve ümmetine bir fazl ü ihsânıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A thousand is the minimum benchmark for abundance, not an exclusive limit; months are used because several reports explain the number by human lifespans or long worship.
rows.anchor: Bu tafdil için asgarî olarak bin adedinin mikyas gösterilmesi tahsis için değil, teksir içindir

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: Mujahid reports that the Prophet mentioned an Israelite soldier armed in God’s cause for a thousand months; the Muslims were amazed and felt their own deeds inadequate, so God revealed the sura.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem Benî İsrâil’den bir erin Allah yolunda bin ay silah giyinmiş olduğunu anlatmıştı

rows.speaker: Ali b. Urve
rows.claim: Ali ibn Urwa reports that the Prophet described four Israelites who worshipped God for eighty years without sinning even for an instant: Job, Zechariah, Hizqil ibn Ajuz, and Joshua ibn Nun; the Companions were amazed and Gabriel brought the sura as better for this community.
rows.anchor: İbn Ebî Hâtim’in Ali b. Urve’den rivayetine göre: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem bir gün Benî İsrâil’den dört kişinin seksen sene Allah’a ibadet edip tarfetü’l-ayn masiyette bulunmadıklarını anlatmış

rows.speaker: İmâm Mâlik
rows.claim: Malik’s Muwatta report says the Prophet worried that his community’s shorter lifespans prevented them from matching earlier peoples’ deeds, so God gave him the Night of Decree, better than a thousand months of other communities.
rows.anchor: İmam Mâlik’in Muvattâ’da zikrettiğine göre, Resûlullah’a ümmetlerin ömürleri gösterilmişti, Resûlullah kendi ümmeti efrâdının ömürlerini kısa addederek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reports explain the thousand-month figure as roughly an exceptionally long, eighty-plus-year lifespan for an individual in this community.
rows.anchor: Bu rivayetlere göre bin ayın tahsîsi seksen küsur senenin bu ümmet içinde bir insan için ekseriyet itibariyle uzun bir ömür olmasına işaret demek olur

rows.speaker: Hasan b. Ali
rows.claim: A report attributed to Hasan ibn Ali says that after his pledge to Muawiya, when a man accused him of disgracing believers, Hasan asked not to be blamed: the Prophet had seen Banu Umayya on his pulpit in a dream, was saddened, and then the Quranic promise of the Night of Decree was revealed.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Hasan b. Ali radıyallâhu anhümâ’ya isnad edilen bir hadis rivayet eylemişler

rows.speaker: Kasım b. Fazl
rows.claim: The narrator Qasim says he calculated the Umayyad reign at exactly one thousand months, neither more nor less.
rows.anchor: bunu rivayet eden Kāsım, “fi’l-vâki‘Benî Ümeyye’nin mülkünü hesab ettik bin ay ediyor, ne ziyade ne eksik” dedi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this interpretation the verse hints at the duration and limited good of the Umayyad state, while also predicting the future miraculously; some infer a Medinan setting because the Prophet’s pulpit was in Medina.
rows.anchor: Buna göre خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍۢ Emeviyye Devleti’nin müddetine ve aynı zamanda onun da bir hayır olduğuna işaret etmiş ve gāibden haber veren bir mucizeyi de tazammun eylemiş oluyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If authentic, the Umayyad report would be the clearest explanation of the thousand months, but its authenticity cannot be established and scholars differ whether it is weak or rejected as munkar.
rows.anchor: Lâkin sıhhati tesbit edilememiş, ancak zayıf mı yoksa münker mi olduğunda ihtilâf edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: Tirmizî
rows.claim: Tirmidhi calls the narration rare and known through this route only; he trusts Qasim, whom Yahya ibn Sa‘id and Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi also endorsed, but says Yusuf ibn Sa‘d is unknown.
rows.anchor: Tirmizî der ki: “Bu bir hadîs-i garîbdir, biz bunu ancak bu vech ile tanıyoruz. Ve Kāsım b. Fadl hadîsinden Yûsuf b. Sa‘d’dan

rows.speaker: Süyûtî
rows.claim: Suyuti notes that the narration has been used to argue the sura is Medinan, but Mizzi called it munkar.
rows.anchor: Süyûtî İtkān’da der ki: “Bu hadis ile sûrenin Medenî olduğuna istidlâl olunuyorsa da

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi cites a Khatib version from Ibn Abbas and Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab saying the Prophet saw Banu Umayya ascend his pulpit in a dream and the Night of Decree sura was then revealed; Suyuti hesitates to call it munkar and settles for weakness.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî’nin naklettiği vechile Hatîb, İbn Abbas’tan da ve kezâ İbn Müseyyeb’den de şu lafız ile tahric eylemiş

rows.speaker: İbn Cerîr
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir says the wording most naturally means that worship on the Night of Decree is better than worship during a thousand months without such a night; he calls alternatives unsupported by transmitted, rational, or scriptural evidence.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr de أَلْفِ شَهْرٍۢ’in tefsîrinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author observes that Ibn Jarir’s ruling effectively rejects the very narrations he had just cited.
rows.anchor: Böyle karar vermek ise rivayet ettiği o haberleri redd ü inkâr demek olduğu cihetle bu da Müzenî’ye iştirak eylemiş demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A thousand months equal 83 years and four months, but counting from Hasan’s transfer of power to Muawiya in 41 AH through Marwan II’s death in 132 AH gives the Umayyad dynasty 91 years and 8–10 months, around a hundred months longer.
rows.anchor: Zira bin ay seksen üç sene dört ay eder.

rows.speaker: Ebû’l-Fidâ
rows.claim: Historians including Ibn al-Athir, Qadi Jamal al-Din, and Abu al-Fida treat the discrepancy as unimportant and accept the report approximately; Abu al-Fida counts fourteen Umayyad caliphs and a reign of just over ninety years, roughly a thousand months.
rows.anchor: Ebu’l-Fidâ şöyle der: “Benî Ümeyye hulefâsı on dörttür; evvelleri Muaviye b. Ebî Süfyan ve âhirleri Mervân-ı Ca‘dî’dir ve mülklerinin müddeti doksan küsur senedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This historical reading treats a thousand months as an approximate sign of the Umayyad state’s bounded duration and good, contrasted with the Night of Decree’s unbounded good; historians’ acceptance answers the arithmetic objection without proving authenticity.
rows.anchor: asıl maksad mefhum, adedi tahkik değil, Benî Ümeyye mülkünün mahdud olan hayriyetine ve müddetine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Qasim claims an exact total, the author gives the precise hadith narrator’s calculation greater weight than historians’ approximation and considers how they might be reconciled.
rows.anchor: muhaddisin[^47] mevsuk bir muhaddis olmak itibariyle tahkīki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First possibility: the report counts the Umayyad rise to power only through Hisham’s death; subtracting the five or six months between Muawiya II’s resignation and Marwan’s accession leaves exactly 83 years and four months.
rows.anchor: Bu ise Hişam b. Abdülmelik ile nihâyet bulmuş, ondan sonraki sekiz sene devr-i inkıraz, yani minberden iniş zamanı olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Second possibility: subtract the roughly nine years when Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr held a rival caliphate after Yazid’s death from the total Umayyad duration; an exact day count may yield the same result.
rows.anchor: Yezid’in vefatı üzerine Abdullah b. Zübeyr Hazretleri’nin mu‘ârız olarak hilâfeti müddeti olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Third possibility: subtract the roughly eight years of rulers regarded as harmful—Yazid I, Yazid II, and Walid II—from the dynasty’s roughly 92 years, leaving about 83 years, so the thousand months can be exact and miraculous.
rows.anchor: birinci Yezid’in zamanında Hazret-i Hüseyin’in şehid edilmesi, dokuzuncuları olan İkinci Yezid b. Abdülmelik’in

rows.speaker: Kādî Abdülcebbar
rows.claim: Abd al-Jabbar objects that the thousand months cannot mean Umayyad rule because their era was blameworthy; calling the Night better than those months implies those months were also good and thus praises them.
rows.anchor: Kādî Abdülcebbar zikrolunan rivayete ta‘n ederek demiştir ki: “Bu bin ayın Benî Ümeyye eyyâmı olması ba‘îddir. Çünkü Benî Ümeyye eyyâmı mezmumdur

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi calls the objection weak: the Umayyad era could be happy in worldly terms while the Night of Decree is far better in religious happiness, so comparison does not make the two equal.
rows.anchor: Râzî de buna karşı demiştir ki: “Bu ta‘n zayıftır. Zira Benî Ümeyye’nin eyyâmı sa‘âdet-i dünyeviye itibariyle büyük günlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite their wrongs, the Umayyads achieved major conquests and restored unity during a period of division; if harmful periods are excluded from the thousand months, the objection also falls away.
rows.anchor: büyük fütûhâtı ve İslâm’ın o sırada geçirmekte olduğu tefrika ve ihtilâl buhranlarının önüne geçerek vahdetinin iadesi gibi dînî, dünyevî hayr u saadet cihetleri de çok olduğu inkâr olunamaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether the Night of Decree is the first revelation night or Badr, its good extending across centuries and states exceeds the best Umayyad days; the report should be read neither solely against nor wholly in favor of the Umayyads.
rows.anchor: leyle-i kadir gerek meşhûru vechile Kur’ân’ın ilk nâzil olduğu nübüvvet gecesi olarak mülâhaza edilsin gerekse Bedir gecesi olsun iki takdirde de onun nice nice asırlara devletlere hâkim olan hayr u bereketi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report remains weak and cannot alone support the interpretation; while allowing the reports as possibilities, the author prefers Ibn Jarir’s general reading that worship on this Night exceeds a thousand months without it, an unlimited special glad tiding to the Prophet and community.
rows.anchor: Onun için en güzel mâna bu rivayetlere ihtimal ile beraber İbn Cerîr’in dediği gibi mutlak olarak leyle-i kadirde amel, leyle-i kadir bulunmayan bin ay amelden daha hayırlıdır diye anlamaktır
